entries.05446f20600a7332: This is a reportable segment that provides solutions optimizing the entire global supply chain of corporate customers by combining international forwarding, international express, contract logistics overseas and other services. Yamato Transport Co., Ltd., Kobe Yamato Co., Ltd., Konan Kogyo Co., Ltd., YAMATO TRANSPORT U.S.A., INC., YAMATO TRANSPORT EUROPE B.V., YAMATO TRANSPORT (S) PTE. LTD., YAMATO TRANSPORT (M) SDN. BHD., Yamato Logistics Management (China) Co., Ltd., Yamato International Logistics Co., Ltd., Yamato Transport (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd., TAIWAN YAMATO INTERNATIONAL LOGISTICS INC. and others are responsible for the segment. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥97,552 million (up 13.5% year on year). The breakdown is logistics support revenue of ¥134,774 million, transportation revenue of ¥6,243 million, other revenue of ¥4,560 million, and intersegment eliminations of −¥48,025 million. The company explains that the increase in revenue was due to progress in expanding international forwarding sales. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥8,150 million, the largest among the reportable segments, a decrease of ¥877 million year on year. Segment assets were ¥62,100 million, and the number of employees was 2,770. The company states that, while leveraging the vast domestic customer base built through Takkyubin, it is working to further expand in areas where it has strengths, such as automotive, high-tech and food industries, and is strengthening its sales capabilities mainly in Japan, North America, China and Southeast Asia. In January 2026, to support the construction of global supply chains for manufacturers aiming to expand production in India, the Yamato Group opened its largest overseas logistics center. Because revenue from external customers in Japan exceeds 90% of consolidated operating revenue, information by region is omitted.

Logistics support revenue of this segment in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥134,774 million (up 15.7% year on year), accounting for most of the segment's revenue. The company says it has put in place a structure in which domestic operating companies and the group's local subsidiaries in each country strengthen cooperation more than ever and promote business as one, and that it worked to improve consolidation efficiency in international forwarding, strengthen proposals to the growing number of cross-border EC operators, and capture logistics demand accompanying domestic demand growth in focus regions. The main overseas companies are located in the United States, Europe, Singapore, Malaysia, China, Hong Kong and Taiwan.

It carries out import and export customs clearance procedures and agency operations for air transport. The company's history records that in January 1951 it concluded an agency agreement with C.A.T. (Civil Air Transport) to begin handling air passenger and cargo, that in August 1958 it concluded an agency agreement with Japan Air Lines Co., Ltd. to begin handling domestic air cargo, and that in February 1960 it began handling international air consolidated cargo. In expanding its business for corporate customers, the company cites customs clearance know-how as a group management resource.

As a foundation for business growth, it says it will promote the use and expansion of integrated business solution bases that combine sorting and transport/delivery functions to logistics bases nationwide with logistics functions. entries.7f2914c048eab1f3: This is a vehicle maintenance service for transport operators. It is run by Yamato Auto Works Co., Ltd., which was established as Daiwa Shoji Co., Ltd. in October 1957 and which was formed in October 2003 by splitting off and integrating the automobile maintenance division of the company's group. The company says that, through a review of business processes, it has promoted an environment in which automobile maintenance technicians can focus on their core work, and that it has worked on expanding sales of the vehicle maintenance service and collecting appropriate fees. The company positions this service as a “vehicle maintenance service that does not stop vehicles and contributes to safe operation by transport operators and to expanding vehicle operating hours.”

entries.94b1f74a1409c735: This is a reportable segment that provides solutions to help corporate customers solve problems and grow their businesses, by combining transportation and delivery networks with added-value functions such as warehouse operations. Yamato Transport Co., Ltd., Nakano Shokai Co., Ltd., IS Tosu Development No. 2 Special Purpose Company and others are responsible for the segment. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥164,602 million (up 69.6% year on year). The breakdown is transportation revenue of ¥54,612 million (up 190.1%), logistics support revenue of ¥117,231 million (up 43.1%), other revenue of ¥16,822 million, and intersegment eliminations of −¥24,063 million. The company explains that this increase in revenue was due to progress in winning new projects and to the conversion of Nakano Shokai Co., Ltd. into a consolidated subsidiary, among other factors. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥6,217 million (up ¥634 million year on year). However, in the current fiscal year, the segment recorded goodwill amortization of ¥14,906 million (of which ¥13,434 million was recorded as "goodwill amortization" in extraordinary losses) in connection with the evaluation of goodwill, and the year-end balance of goodwill fell from ¥15,827 million at the end of the prior year to ¥920 million. The segment also recorded an impairment loss on fixed assets of ¥1,030 million. Segment assets were ¥99,913 million, the number of employees was 7,603, and capital expenditure was ¥15,745 million, including construction of logistics facilities and renovation work at various bases. In October 2025, the company opened an integrated business solutions base in Koriyama City, Fukushima Prefecture, which combines a transport terminal of the Yamato Group with a logistics center that has high added-value functions.

entries.b0145c58008477e4: This is a category listed under Express Business among the types of services by reportable segment. Apart from small-scale parcel delivery, it transports cargo by truck. In May 2024, the company established Sustainable Shared Transport Co., Ltd., which provides an open platform for shared transportation and delivery. The company states that it is advancing the development of this open platform for shared transportation and delivery, in which diverse stakeholders participate.
entries.b4ffec0e6c754935: This reportable segment provides vehicle maintenance services that support safe operation by transport operators and expand vehicle operating hours without stopping vehicles, and supplies renewable electricity and other power used for EVs. It is run by Yamato Auto Works Co., Ltd., its regional companies (Iwate, Hokushinetsu, Shikoku and Okinawa), and Yamato Energy Management Co., Ltd. Operating revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥22,033 million (up 7.5% year on year), which the company attributes to an increase in the number of contracted vehicles as well as the collection of appropriate fees. Intersegment internal operating revenue or transfers amounted to ¥44,401 million, and operating revenue including these was ¥66,435 million, a structure in which vehicle maintenance within the group accounts for a large share. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥5,221 million (up ¥1,440 million year on year), which the company attributes to, among other things, its focus on optimizing costs. Segment assets were ¥53,959 million, and the number of employees was 1,996. The company says it is promoting sales of the “EV Life Cycle Service,” which packages, in addition to vehicle maintenance services, know-how on EV procurement and efficient use, the supply of renewable energy-derived electricity, and the energy management system developed within the Yamato Group, drawing on know-how in EVs, solar power generation equipment and energy management that it has accumulated through environmental investment and demonstration projects within the Yamato Group.

entries.c1e641d814e7d8c4: Home delivery of small-lot cargo centered on "Takkyubin." Handling volume in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was 1,941 million units for Takkyubin, Takkyubin Compact and EAZY (down 1.0% from the previous fiscal year), 451 million units for Nekopos and Kuroneko Yu-Packet (up 15.4%), and 95 million copies for Kuroneko Yu-Mail (down 13.6%). In the related information "Information by product and service," operating revenues from external customers are divided into ¥1,408,896 million for home delivery and ¥456,778 million for others. The company focuses on creating an environment in which sales drivers can devote themselves to facing customers and providing better service, and is advancing the relocation of collection and delivery bases based on regional market potential and the rollout of community-based service bases that offer services beyond sending and receiving Takkyubin. Expanding the provision of the "leave-at-door" service in cooperation with EC operators is also cited as an initiative that contributes to reducing redelivery, making logistics more efficient and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The company states that although the home delivery market is on an expanding trend along with the growth of EC, the market for individuals and small-lot corporate customers, its base area, is affected by population decline and weak personal consumption, and the profitability of the Takkyubin network is on a declining trend.
entries.ca79ede9911482f6: This category supports efforts to expand the value provided across customers' entire supply chains, through functions held by the Yamato Group such as IT, call centers and financial services. The securities report lists four reportable segments: “Express Business,” “Contract Logistics Business,” “Global Business” and “Mobility Business.” Because this category is not included in the reportable segments, it is shown here even though its operating revenue from external customers exceeds that of the Mobility Business. It includes Yamato System Development Co., Ltd., Yamato Contact Service Co., Ltd., Yamato Credit Finance Co., Ltd., MY MEDICA Co., Ltd., Yamato Staff Supply Co., Ltd., Yamato Lease Co., Ltd. and others. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, operating revenue from external customers was ¥23,507 million (down 3.9% year on year), operating revenue including intersegment amounts was ¥66,369 million, segment profit (operating profit) was ¥6,629 million (down ¥1,571 million year on year), segment assets were ¥114,300 million, and the number of employees was 4,407. The company says it has promoted the provision of IT services that contribute to improving customers' operational efficiency and end users' convenience. The securities report also states that, at the board of directors meeting held on May 14, 2026, the transfer of all shares of Yamato Credit Finance Co., Ltd. held by the company was approved, effective September 1, 2026, and that it is scheduled to cease to be a subsidiary.

entries.cdd58225a428844e: This is a service that packages know-how on EV procurement and efficient use, the supply of renewable energy-derived electricity, and the energy management system developed within the Yamato Group. In October 2024 it began the “EV Life Cycle Service” for businesses that use vehicles, and in January 2025 it established Yamato Energy Management Co., Ltd., which supplies renewable energy-derived electricity and other power. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, it strengthened its sales structure and is promoting sales expansion. To achieve “net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 2050 (own emissions)” and “a 48% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 (compared with the fiscal year ended March 2021),” the company says it is promoting measures such as “introducing EVs,” “introducing solar power generation equipment” and “increasing the use of renewable energy-derived electricity,” and it provides the know-how accumulated through these measures to outside parties as a “Green Mobility” business model.
